criteria.text: Opioid withdrawal mitigation to facilitate abrupt opioid discontinuation
Patient is at least 18 years old.
Confirmed opioid dependence or opioid use disorder
Prescribed by or in consultation with a pain management or addiction specialist
Undergoing or scheduled to undergo abrupt opioid discontinuation

At least one: tried and failed clonidine within the last 6 months, contraindication to clonidine, clinically significant adverse effect from clonidine, or Lucemyra initiated in the emergency department.

notes: Partial encoding of archived Alaska Medicaid Lucemyra (lofexidine) opioid-withdrawal criteria, effective 2019-03-11.

Encoded: closed opioid withdrawal mitigation indication and all six approval requirements. Denials mirror approval failures: age under 18, no confirmed opioid dependence or opioid use disorder, no qualifying specialist prescribing or consultation, no abrupt opioid discontinuation planned or underway, abnormal QT interval, or none of the clonidine/ED paths.
Cautions (notes only): risk of hypotension, bradycardia and syncope; patients with prolonged QT intervals should avoid Lucemyra; concomitant CNS depressants increase the risk of CNS depression.
Cautions (notes only): hepatic or renal impairment may require dose adjustment; taper over 2–4 days on discontinuation.
Duration (notes only): initial approval 7 days (112 tablets); reauthorization 7 days (112 tablets) with documentation of positive patient response. Treatment for 3–7 days is often sufficient.
Quantity (notes only): 112 tablets per 7 days; maximum 14 days per month; maximum three 14-day treatments per year. max_units is null.

Clinical facts are attestations. Documentation verification, cautions, duration, positive response on reauthorization, and quantity enforcement require manual review. PDL status unknown; no linked alternatives.
